laws.rule: Tourists visiting the Raja Ampat Islands marine protected area must pay a regional levy (TLPJL, the environmental service fee) through the official kkprajaampat.id service or the manager's service counter; the electronic TLPJL is emailed after payment is verified. Verified payments are generally not refundable.

layers.authority: UPTD for the Management of the Raja Ampat Islands Marine Protected Area, under the Southwest Papua Province marine and fisheries agency
layers.process: A visitor to the Raja Ampat Islands marine protected area books and pays the TLPJL (Environmental Services Maintenance Service Tariff, a regional levy that works as an entrance ticket) through the official website or the manager's service counter. The booking is complete only after payment is verified and the TLPJL is issued; its validity follows the period printed on it. The rate shown in the payment system follows the regional regulation in force on the payment date, so the amount is not repeated here. Visitors must be 18 or over, or have a parent or guardian's consent. Group bookings of more than five people may need the manager's data format.

layers.authority: Government of Indonesia (as reported by Smartraveller)
layers.process: Smartraveller says you may need a travel permit (Surat Keterangan Jalan) to visit some areas of the Papua provinces. Check whether one applies with the nearest Indonesian embassy or consulate, or with your travel provider. Smartraveller doesn't say which areas, who issues it or how long it takes, so none of that is confirmed here.
